title: Moonshine

cover_image.note: Flat front cover from twelve-books.com's listing of the MACK edition; MACK's own product image (cdn.shopify.com/s/files/1/0035/7439/9040/products/cover95.jpg) is an angled product shot of the same cover.

description.main: Bertien van Manen's Moonshine gathers almost thirty years of photographs made with mining families in the Appalachian mountains of Kentucky, Tennessee and West Virginia, from a first visit in 1985 to a last in 2013. MACK published it in 2014.
description.extended:
Bertien van Manen's Moonshine gathers almost thirty years of photographs of mining families in the Appalachian mountains of Kentucky, Tennessee and West Virginia, made between a first visit in 1985 and a last in 2013.

Van Manen lived with the people she photographed. The Boggs family and their ten red-haired sons recur, as do the miners Mavis and Junior, children doing handstands on a couch, a daughter combing her grandmother's hair. The pictures stay close to the body and the room. Around them the region changes: mines close and families leave wooden cabins for town or for trailer parks. Early black-and-white frames sit beside later colour work, so time shows in the printing as well as the faces. MACK published the book in 2014 as a 112-page cloth hardcover with a tipped-in image on the front board.

Van Manen (1935-2024) was born in The Hague. She began in fashion photography and turned to long documentary projects made with small cameras after reading Robert Frank's The Americans, among them A Hundred Summers, A Hundred Winters on the former Soviet Union and East Wind West Wind on China. Moonshine was her third book with MACK, after Let's Sit Down Before We Go (2011) and Easter and Oak Trees (2013).
description.artist_bio: Bertien van Manen (The Hague 1935 - Amsterdam 2024), Dutch documentary photographer. Began in fashion photography in 1974; turned to documentary work after encountering Robert Frank's The Americans. Books include A Hundred Summers, A Hundred Winters (1994), East Wind West Wind (2001), Give Me Your Image (Steidl 2006), Let's Sit Down Before We Go (MACK 2011), Easter and Oak Trees (MACK 2013), Moonshine (MACK 2014), Beyond Maps and Atlases (MACK 2016), I Will Be Wolf (MACK 2017), Archive (MACK 2019), Gluckauf (2023). Collections: Stedelijk Museum, Rijksmuseum, FOMU Antwerp, MEP Paris, Fotomuseum Winterthur, MoMA, Metropolitan Museum, SFMOMA.
description.exhibition_context: Moonshine was shown at Robert Morat, Paris Photo 2014; Yancey Richardson, New York, 2014; Annet Gelink Gallery, Amsterdam, 2021; SCHUNCK, Heerlen (collection acquisition), 2021.
